title: Return Values
objective: Send a value back from a function with return and use it in the caller.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A function that only calls console.log() shows its output directly on screen — nothing comes back to the code that called it. return sends a value back instead, so the caller can store it, check it, or pass it somewhere else.
As soon as JavaScript executes a return statement, the function stops immediately — any code written after it in that function never runs, even if it's still inside the function body.

A function without an explicit return statement returns undefined, JavaScript's way of saying 'nothing.' Logging and returning solve different problems: logging is for showing a human something right now; returning is for handing a value to the rest of the program.
explanation.rule: return sends a value back to the caller and immediately ends the function — code after it never runs.

examples.title: Using a Returned Value
examples.note: double() hands back a value, which is stored in result and logged afterward — it never logs anything itself.

checks.question: function greet() { console.log("hi"); } — what does greet() return, since it has no return statement?

feedback.correct: Correct — a function with no return statement returns undefined.
feedback.incorrect: A function that never hits a return statement automatically returns undefined, not null or an error.

assignment.title: Temper the Blade
assignment.brief: Write temperRating(hardness) that returns 'brittle' if hardness > 60, 'tempered' if hardness >= 30, otherwise 'soft'. Log the returned value for temperRating(45).
requirements: Return 'brittle' for hardness > 60, 'tempered' for hardness >= 30, otherwise 'soft'.

hints: Check the highest threshold first: hardness > 60 gives 'brittle'.
temperRating(45) should return 'tempered', since 45 is at least 30 but not over 60.
